chunks: Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Uthman ibn Isa and al-Hasan ibn Mahbub all together, from Sama'a, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who was answered oppositely by two of his co-religionists in regards to a matter – both transmitting it, one of them obligates it while the other forbids it – what should he do?
He said: He withholds [doing anything] until he accesses one who will inform him, and he is respited until such a time as he meets him.
And in another narration: Whichever of them you act by – if done in subservience – suffices you.

key_terms.وَسِعَكَ: it suffices you / is sufficient for you

ai.seo_question: What should a Muslim do when two scholars give contradictory rulings on the same issue?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the jurisprudential issue of conflicting narrations (ikhtilaf al-riwayat) where two authorities provide opposite rulings on the same matter. The Imam advises postponing action until a definitive answer is found, but also offers a secondary opinion that acting on either ruling with the intention of obedience is sufficient.

en.ammaar-muslim: 1. [1/-] al-Kafi: Ali b. Ibrahim from his father from Uthman b. Isa and al-Hasan b. Mahbub all together from Sama’a from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, he (Sama’a) said:

I asked him about a man who is answered oppositely by two of his co-religionists (i.e. Shi’as) in regards to a matter – both transmitting it [their answers – on your authority], one of them obligates it while the other forbids it – what should he do?
he said: he withholds [doing anything] until he accesses one who will inform him (of the true position), and he is respited until such a time as he meets him.
[And in another narration [the Imam said]: whichever of them you act by – suffices you – if done in subservience (with the intention of obeying)].
